answer_raw:
Your US accounts will generally remain under US jurisdiction, but your Brazilian apartment and any Brazilian bank accounts will be subject to Brazilian law and inheritance processes.

**Brazilian assets** — including real estate, local bank accounts, and investments located in Brazil — are governed by the **Brazilian Civil Code** regardless of where the heirs live or where the deceased was a citizen [4]. This means your heirs in the US will have to navigate a Brazilian inheritance process (probate) to settle the apartment and local accounts [4]. If you have a will, it must typically be validated by a Brazilian authority or judge to ensure it meets local formal requirements [7].

**US-situated assets** — such as your US-based bank accounts — are subject to **US estate tax** rules. If the value of your US-situated assets (combined with previous taxable gifts) exceeds the filing threshold of **$60,000 as of June 2026** [6], your executor must file **Form 706-NA** within nine months of your death [6]. While Brazilian assets are handled in Brazil, your US accounts are handled in the US, though you may use a **Foreign Tax Credit** (Form 1116) to mitigate double taxation if certain taxes were paid to Brazil [8].

I didn't find the exact interaction between Brazilian inheritance tax and US estate tax for a resident non-citizen, so you should consult a cross-border tax attorney to see how much of the Brazilian tax can be credited against US obligations.
